title: Harness active-model scoping (T1 core)
desc: T1 core: scope every gate/score/pace to WHO works now (active model via wkagent-name) and WHETHER a human watches. 8 principle NAMES only -- HOW => harness-active-model-scoping-howto, dated incidents+impl history => harness-active-model-scoping-ref.
steps: THESIS: scope every gate / score / pace to WHO is working NOW (active model resolved via wkagent-name -- process-chain, not the spoofable env var) and WHETHER a human is watching (transcript-derived state, no marker files). This T1 lists the principle NAMES; implementation HOW => harness-active-model-scoping-howto; the dated incidents that birthed each + impl-status history => harness-active-model-scoping-ref.

P1 skill-comments by VERIFIED identity (author=wkagent-name, stored out-of-body). P2 cheap-model-comprehension raises author score (declared-tier transfer-quiz). P3 PACE IS ACTIVE-MODEL-SCOPED not global -- a delegated agent spends ITS OWN quota; gate on NEAR-CAP, not the linear-elapsed target. P4 STALL resets on a user turn (DONE 2026-06-09).

P5 GATE-AS-SIGN: every block/suggest/skill-id names a VERIFIED working escape + one-line why, never a dead-end. P6 every guard points to its OWN same-named skill (<name>-guard), not a generic dump. P7 cheap models edit ONLY sandbox/-proto/gitignored; ROOT (Opus/Sonnet/pro) merges to canonical; harness .ps1 = ROOT-only. P8 a pace FAMILY = a CLI tool (Claude/Codex/Gemini/Agy/GPT/Groq), per-model WITHIN; refresh a >1h-stale family cache immediately from its live source.

WHEN TO USE: read before touching any pace/stall/tier gate or score, before a delegation pace decision, or whenever a guard MIS-FIRES (it is probably scoped to the wrong WHO/WHETHER). CROSS: wkagent-name-tool, opus-mechanical-self-drag-antipattern, pace-deadlock-escapes-harness-editable-and-jisikhwa-free, business-hours-triage-emergency-first. TARGET ARCH: wkpace becomes the single per-CLI-family pace engine and the harness gates REFERENCE it (no duplicate pace math).

PACE FAMILY DISPLAY FORMAT (2026-06-12): When showing token usage in wkpace / doctor, always display the cap denominator in the same unit as the numerator. If used=4.9K tokens, show cap as 500K not 500000K. Pattern: [math]::Round(tokVar/1e3,1))K/[math]::Round(capVar/1e3,0))K. The cap variable holds raw tokens (500000), not already-K-divided. Groq cap=500000 (500K/day), Cerebras cap=1000000 (1M/day). These are faint-calibratable defaults based on API docs; user can override by editing the variable in wkpace.ps1.
